tool.name: BeeGees
tool.command:
python3 << PYEOF import csv
## Load optional metadata (ID -> taxonomy dict) meta = {} #if $metadata with open('${metadata}', newline='') as f: for row in csv.DictReader(f): meta[row['ID']] = row #end if
tax_cols = ['phylum', 'class', 'order', 'family', 'genus', 'species']
#if $run_mode.mode == 'PE' base_cols = ['ID', 'R1', 'R2'] rows = [ #for $el in $run_mode.reads {'ID': '${el.name}', 'R1': '${el.forward}', 'R2': '${el.reverse}'}, #end for ] #else base_cols = ['ID', 'R1'] rows = [ #for $el in $run_mode.reads {'ID': '${el.name}', 'R1': '${el}'}, #end for ] #end if
fieldnames = base_cols + (tax_cols if meta else []) with open('samples.csv', 'w', newline='') as out: w = csv.DictWriter(out, fieldnames=fieldnames, extrasaction='ignore') w.writeheader() for row in rows: if meta and row['ID'] in meta: row.update({c: meta[row['ID']].get(c, '') for c in tax_cols}) w.writerow({k: row.get(k, '') for k in fieldnames}) PYEOF && beegees run --config '$config_file' --profile local --cores \${GALAXY_SLOTS:-4} #if $log_file --log-file '$log_out' #end if && zip -rj '$plots_zip' beegees_output/05_barcoding_outcome/plots/

param.name: reads
param.label: Paired-end reads (list:paired collection)
param.help: Build a list:paired collection from your history using the Rule Builder for large sample sets.

param.name: metadata
param.label: Sample metadata CSV (optional)
param.help: Columns: ID, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species. ID must match collection element identifiers exactly. Required when using gene-fetch with hierarchical input.

validator.message: Must be a valid e-mail address

param.name: api_key
param.label: NCBI API key
param.help: Obtain from your NCBI account settings.

param.name: input_type
param.label: Taxonomy input type in samples CSV

param.name: genbank
param.label: Download GenBank records for retrieved references

param.name: adapter_r1
param.label: R1 adapter sequence (PE; leave empty for Illumina default)

param.name: adapter_r2
param.label: R2 adapter sequence (PE; leave empty for Illumina default)

param.name: n
param.label: bp to extend beyond Exonerate alignment (n)

param.name: C
param.label: Genetic code table (C)
param.help: NCBI genetic code number; 5 = invertebrate mitochondrial.

param.name: reference_dir
param.label: Reference FASTA for filtering
param.help: Single FASTA file used as the reference directory source.

validator.message: No BLAST databases are installed. Ask your Galaxy admin, or switch to 'Upload FASTA from history'.

param.name: blast_db_file
param.label: BLAST database FASTA file
param.help: Will be used directly as the BLASTn subject database.

validator.message: No taxonomy tables are installed. Ask your Galaxy admin, or switch to 'Upload TSV from history'.

param.name: db_taxonomy_file
param.label: Taxonomy TSV
param.help: Must contain columns: ID, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species (tab-separated).

param.name: expected_taxonomy
param.label: Expected taxonomy CSV (optional)
param.help: Must contain columns: ID, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species.

tool.help:
**BeeGees** recovers DNA barcodes from low-coverage genome skim data.
It wraps the following pipeline steps:
1. **fastp** — adapter trimming and QC (paired-end merge + concat, or single-end) 2. **gene-fetch** (optional) — downloads per-sample reference sequences from NCBI 3. **MitoGeneExtractor** — protein-guided barcode extraction across an r×s parameter sweep 4. **fasta_cleaner** — removes human contamination, AT outliers, statistical outliers, and optional custom-reference contaminants 5. **Structural validation** — HMM + reading-frame + stop-codon checks 6. **Taxonomic validation** — BLASTn against a local database with hierarchical taxonomic matching 7. **MultiQC** — aggregated QC report
**Samples CSV format** (``.csv``, comma-separated)
.. warning::
Sample IDs must **not contain underscores**. The pipeline uses ``_`` as an internal delimiter to separate sample IDs from parameter suffixes in output filenames. Use hyphens (``-``) instead (e.g. ``sample-001``).
For paired-end runs supply columns ``ID``, ``R1``, ``R2`` (and optionally taxonomy columns). For single-end runs omit ``R2``. When using ``gene-fetch`` with ``input_type=hierarchical``, include the taxonomy columns shown below.
*Paired-end example*:
.. csv-table:: :header: ID,R1,R2,phylum,class,order,family,genus,species
sample-001,/data/s001-R1.fastq.gz,/data/s001-R2.fastq.gz,Arthropoda,Insecta,Coleoptera,Carabidae,Carabus,Carabus coriaceus sample-002,/data/s002-R1.fastq.gz,/data/s002-R2.fastq.gz,Arthropoda,Insecta,Lepidoptera,Nymphalidae,Vanessa,Vanessa atalanta sample-003,/data/s003-R1.fastq.gz,/data/s003-R2.fastq.gz,Arthropoda,Insecta,Diptera,Drosophilidae,Drosophila,Drosophila melanogaster
*Single-end (SE / Ultima) example*:
.. csv-table:: :header: ID,R1,phylum,class,order,family,genus,species
sample-001,/data/s001.fastq.gz,Arthropoda,Insecta,Coleoptera,Carabidae,Carabus,Carabus coriaceus sample-002,/data/s002.fastq.gz,Arthropoda,Insecta,Lepidoptera,Nymphalidae,Vanessa,Vanessa atalanta sample-003,/data/s003.fastq.gz,Arthropoda,Insecta,Diptera,Drosophilidae,Drosophila,Drosophila melanogaster
----
**BLAST database**
Select a database pre-installed by your Galaxy admin, or upload a FASTA file from your history (the pipeline will build the BLAST index automatically). The sequence IDs in the database must match those in the taxonomy TSV below.
See `docs/README_custom_blast_dbs.md <https://github.com/bge-barcoding/BeeGees/blob/main/docs/README_custom_blast_dbs.md>`_ for instructions on building a custom database.
**Taxonomy TSV** (``.tsv``, tab-separated)
Two formats are accepted — see the `custom BLAST DB docs <https://github.com/bge-barcoding/BeeGees/blob/main/docs/README_custom_blast_dbs.md#taxonomy-tsv-file-formats>`_ for full details.
*Format A — generic (``Feature ID`` + semicolon-delimited lineage)*::
Feature ID Taxon MH021436.1 k__Viridiplantae;p__Streptophyta;c__Magnoliopsida;o__Solanales;f__Solanaceae;g__Solanum;s__Solanum bukasovii
*Format B — BOLDistilled-style (one column per rank)*::
bin kingdom phylum class order family genus species MH021436.1 Viridiplantae Streptophyta Magnoliopsida Solanales Solanaceae Solanum Solanum bukasovii
The sequence ID in the taxonomy file must exactly match the hit ID returned by BLAST (``sseqid``).
